seo.title: Underfloor Heating Installation in Windsor | Install My Bathroom
seo.description: Fit-only underfloor heating for Windsor bathrooms, from narrow-plot Georgian town houses near the Castle to post-war family homes further out.

hero.intro: Windsor's housing splits fairly cleanly into two character types: close to the Castle and the historic centre, Georgian and Victorian town houses on narrow plots with limited rear access; further out, inter-war and post-war family homes and newer residential developments. Underfloor heating works in both, but the practical constraints of getting materials in and a system fitted are very different depending on which part of Windsor you're in.

sections.heading: Narrow town houses near the Castle: access is the real constraint
sections.body: Many properties close to the Castle sit on narrow plots with limited rear access and period staircases that constrain how much material can be moved through the building at once. That's as relevant to underfloor heating as it is to any other part of a bathroom strip-out: insulation boards, bags of screed or self-levelling compound, and rolls of heating mat all have to go up a narrow period staircase in manageable loads rather than arrive as one bulk delivery. These town houses are also more likely to have a suspended timber floor beneath the bathroom, so we check joist condition and span before fitting a rigid insulation-backed board to carry a low-profile electric mat — the system that adds the least height and the fewest heavy deliveries, which matters when every bag has to be carried up by hand.

sections.heading: Further out: post-war homes and newer developments give more flexibility
sections.body: Inter-war and post-war family homes on the edges of Windsor, along with newer residential developments on redeveloped sites, are more likely to have wider access and a solid concrete ground floor. That opens up a screeded water-fed underfloor heating system tied into the existing central heating as a realistic option alongside electric, and makes material access far more straightforward than in the older town houses nearer the centre.

sections.heading: Floor height allowance applies either way
sections.body: Whichever part of Windsor you're in, underfloor heating adds to the existing floor depth — insulation, then the heating mat or pipe, then screed or board, then tile adhesive and tile. Totals typically run from around 15mm for a thin electric mat system up to 70mm or more for a screeded water-fed one. In a narrow Georgian or Victorian town house, that height change needs checking carefully against period skirting, door architraves and staircases that weren't built with modern floor build-ups in mind; in a newer property, there's usually more tolerance.

sections.heading: How we run the job
sections.body: At survey we confirm floor type, access constraints and the right system. We then strip the existing floor back, check and make good joists or slab, lay insulation, fit and test the mat or pipe, cover it with screed or board, and hand over to tiling. The thermostat is wired in, commissioned and tested, and we snag the finished room before handover.

faqs.q: Can underfloor heating be fitted in a narrow Georgian town house near Windsor Castle?
faqs.a: Yes, but access shapes the approach. Materials go up period staircases in manageable loads, and we typically specify a low-profile electric mat over an insulation-backed board, which keeps deliveries and added floor height to a minimum.

faqs.q: Is water-fed underfloor heating an option in Windsor?
faqs.a: It usually suits the newer, wider-access properties further from the centre with a solid concrete floor, where a screeded system tied into the existing central heating is more straightforward to fit.

faqs.q: Will underfloor heating cause problems with period skirting or door architraves?
faqs.a: It can if the added floor height isn't planned for. We check the expected build-up against period skirting, architraves and staircases at survey stage, particularly in town houses near the Castle.

faqs.q: How much extra height does underfloor heating add to a Windsor bathroom floor?
faqs.a: Typically 15mm to 70mm depending on the system, once insulation, the heating element, screed or board, and tile are accounted for.

faqs.q: Do you check access before quoting for a central Windsor property?
faqs.a: Yes. The £125 survey covers both the floor type and how materials will get in and up to the bathroom, which matters more in narrow period town houses than in newer developments.
